note: OBSERVED gate runtimes in ms. Written by tools/ship/selfchecks.mjs on a full run and read by gateBudget-selfcheck, which compares the recorded SLOWEST_GENERAL against what was actually seen. IT SHIPS WITH DATA rather than empty: a check fed by a file nobody has produced is a control that cannot fail, and this one exists precisely because the previous budget rule lived in a comment.
captured: v3211 full-suite run (556 gates) plus the quiet-box tail measured with a 300s ceiling; plus 13 gates added in the v3285 session, each timed individually on this box (not batch wall-clock -- the first pass through this round attached the word MEASURED to estimates that a re-measure contradicted by up to 20x); plus the 15 gates added v3567-v3583, EACH TIMED INDIVIDUALLY on this box following the v3285 precedent rather than batch wall-clock. placementRender was timed WITH jsdom INSTALLED (7.6s): without it the gate SKIPS in 39ms, and recording a skip as a runtime would have put a 39ms budget on a 7.6s check. ; plus 24 gates timed individually at v3924 -- the clean-passing part of a 55-gate sweep of everything that had NEITHER a recorded time NOR a MEASURED budget. Twelve of those 55 exceeded a 150s cap and are NOT here: a gate that does not complete leaves no entry, which is the reason this file could never show an over-budget gate and why 'zero over default' was a property of the file rather than of the tree. Nineteen more exited nonzero and are excluded by the same rule that has always excluded failures. ; and at v3925 placementRender was re-timed WITH jsdom PRESENT: 14057ms, replacing a recorded 54ms that was its SKIP time. The gate reports cleanly and exits 0 when jsdom is absent, so the writer recorded a measurement of the check declining to run -- 54ms as the budget for a 14s check, which the first timeout would have made look like a hang in something that is fine. jsdom is a dev dependency, npm i jsdom --no-save, as that gate's own header says. ; and at v3941 the SKIP-TIME REGRESSION WAS FIXED AT ITS CAUSE RATHER THAN RE-TIMED A THIRD TIME. placementRender had been recorded at its skip time twice before (54ms, found and re-timed to 14057ms at v3925) and was back at 43ms. The cause was never the number: selfchecks.mjs recorded elapsed time on the SUCCESS path, and a gate that skips exits 0, so its skip time was written and MERGED over the real measurement every time its dependency went missing on the timing box. Failures and timeouts were excluded; skips were not, because a skip looks exactly like a fast pass. selfchecks now reads the skip line every skipping gate in this tree was already printing and leaves those runs OUT of the record, saying so in the summary. Measured, not assumed: 40 gates here can skip, and 3 of them were holding a skip time as their budget evidence -- placementRender (43ms), holoPicture (55ms), holoAgree (56ms). The other 19 sub-200ms entries among skippable gates are genuinely fast and were left alone. placementRender is re-timed here WITH jsdom installed: 12513ms, the median of 12641/12513/12310. holoPicture and holoAgree are REMOVED rather than guessed -- both skip for want of a rasteriser this box cannot supply, and an absent entry and a skip time are different claims. magmapTaichi was timed individually on this box at v3941: 44ms, the median of 44/44/46 -- it is a static gate over vendored source and a kernel string, and deliberately runs nothing on a device. gateConfigWrites was also timed individually at v3941: 129ms, the median of 129/130/121. It arrived at v3937 and had never been timed -- it was the last gate in the tree carrying no runtime evidence of any kind. cloneSource was timed individually at v3941: 60ms, the median of 60/58/60 -- it drives the pure parse helpers and reads source, and deliberately performs no clone of its own. githubPanelLive was timed individually at v3941: 3540ms, the median of 3540/3432/3541 -- it launches a real headless Chromium and drives the GitHub panel end to end, so its cost is real browser time rather than source scanning. Missed when the gate was first added and closed a round late, the same way gateConfigWrites and magmapTaichi were. ; and at v3964 the THIRTEEN GATES ADDED IN THE v3944-v3964 SESSION were each timed INDIVIDUALLY on this box, median of three runs, following the v3285 precedent rather than batch wall-clock: firewallBanner 6724 (6794/6681/6724), releaseWorkflow 44 (45/44/39), sharpBridge 331 (327/331/334), recordFloat 3382 (3382/3378/3386), routeShadow 260 (260/265/259), bridgeWiring 470 (491/470/470), pageSectionsReport 1155 (1216/1155/1150), chipOrder 1386 (1431/1386/1382), pageGround 3002 (3016/2982/3002), magmapTaichiRun 876 (935/866/876), magmapBenchVerdict 3468 (3523/3468/3402), sharpPanel 11433 (11458/11433/11381), sourceChain 162 (164/159/162). Eight of the thirteen launch a real headless Chromium, so their cost is browser time rather than source scanning -- sharpPanel is the slowest because it loads server.html NINE times, once per scenario, which is the price of driving refusals instead of describing them. EVERY ONE WAS TIMED PASSING: sourceChain exited 1 on its first timing pass because the run BEFORE it had rewired the bridge's dispatch from a local alias to its own name (to satisfy bridgeCensus), and that gate's own check still named the alias. It was fixed and re-timed rather than recorded red -- a failing run's elapsed time is not a budget. ; and at v3965 magmapDefault was timed individually on this box: 721ms, the median of 721/698/769. It launches a real headless Chromium with WebGPU and runs the magmap kernel FOUR times (the new default, the kernel it replaced, the above-cap fallback, and the shared kernel forced past its cap to prove the guard is load-bearing), so its cost is GPU time rather than source scanning. ; and at v3966 magmapTaichiRun was RE-TIMED after gaining the batched-path checks: 1033ms, the median of 1071/1033/1011, up from 876ms. Re-timed rather than left alone because a gate that grew four checks and kept its old number is carrying evidence about a version of itself that no longer exists. ; and at v3967 nodeBunPage was timed individually: 170ms, the median of 168/170/172. Static-only (no browser launch), which is why it is fast despite the page it checks spawning real processes when a human clicks its buttons. ; and at v3968 brain/rl/lessons-selfcheck was timed individually: 49ms, the median of 70/49/49. It drives the real watchdog to both recorded verdicts and writes to a scratch JSONL in os.tmpdir(), so it touches no browser and no GPU. ; and at v3969 lessons-selfcheck was re-timed after gaining the read-side and observer checks: 52ms, the median of 51/52/51. ; and at v3970 lessons-selfcheck was re-timed again after gaining the recordSweepFinding checks: 61ms, the median of 54/69/61. ; and at v3972 levelClaim was RE-TIMED on this box after being wired into the lesson corpus: 770000ms WIRED, against 768000ms UNWIRED measured immediately before the wiring on the same box, replacing a recorded 646938ms from a different box. BOTH ARMS WERE RUN IN FULL rather than the wired one alone -- the round's whole claim is that reading and writing the corpus changes no physics verdict, and the two outputs are BYTE-IDENTICAL with only the [lessons] header line differing, which is evidence rather than an assurance. The +2s is the read of an 8-record JSONL, and the corpus was VERIFIED UNCHANGED after the wired run (still 8 records, no sph-level entry) because levelClaim is green and a sweep that settled writes nothing. It is the most expensive gate in the tree and a gate that grew two write sites while keeping its old number would be carrying evidence about a version of itself that no longer exists. lessons-selfcheck was re-timed after gaining the levelClaim wiring checks: 61ms, the median of 61/60/63 -- UNCHANGED from v3970, recorded anyway because 'the number did not move' is a measurement and 'nobody looked' is not. ; and at v3973 sensitivity-selfcheck was timed to completion for the FIRST TIME on this box: 170384ms, the median of 176873/170384/156443, every run GREEN. It had been in gateBudget's UNRESOLVED table since v3924 ('exceeded a 150s cap; never timed before that') and is DELETED from it here rather than left sitting in both. The measurement is the point of the round: for as long as it ran over the ~140s default the suite SIGTERMed it, so the REAL failure it was carrying -- 11 dead knobs against a cap of 8, ten of which were alive -- could never print. A TIMEOUT IS NOT A FAILURE, which is how a gate stays red for fifty rounds without anyone knowing. The 13% spread across three runs (156s-177s) is recorded rather than hidden: the cost is 30 devices x every mode x every knob and several of those devices are iterative. Median written down, 2x tail headroom covers the rest. ; and at v3974 packingTransfer was RE-TIMED after being wired into the lesson corpus: 225000ms WIRED, the median of 227/225/224s, against 223s UNWIRED measured immediately before the wiring on the same box. Both arms run in full and their outputs are BYTE-IDENTICAL apart from the [lessons] header, verified across TWO separate wired runs. It replaces a recorded 186634ms from a different box, and it is re-timed rather than left alone because the gate grew a read and two write sites. The +2s is a read of a 10-record JSONL. lessons-selfcheck re-timed after gaining the packingTransfer and dedup checks: 61ms, unchanged. ; and at v3975 materialKnobs was RE-TIMED after being wired into the lesson corpus: 154400ms WIRED, the median of 155000/154356/154000ms across three full runs on this box (two of them driving real writes, the third confirming dedup held the corpus at 12 records), against 154000ms UNWIRED measured immediately before the wiring. Both arms are BYTE-IDENTICAL apart from the [lessons] header. It replaces a recorded 132632ms from a different box.
failingNote: RUNTIMES OF GATES THAT COMPLETED AND EXITED NONZERO, recorded at v3924 and kept OUT of `timings` because the writer has always excluded failures -- a gate that fails early has not exercised its full path, so its time understates. They are recorded HERE because a red verdict is not the same fact as an unknown runtime, and folding the two together is how nineteen failing gates stayed invisible: none of them had ever been timed, so nothing in the tree had a reason to run them. THIS MAP IS EVIDENCE ABOUT DURATION, NOT A SUPPRESSION OF THE FAILURE -- the failures are real, they are listed here by name, and they are the next round's work.
